business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global Export Distribution of High-Proof Traditional Sorghum Baijiu

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (Arab Republic of Egypt) – unitary national jurisdiction; Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) available as strategic export platform
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (mixed; Islamic Sharia as source of legislation per Article 2 of the 2014 Constitution); unitary national system
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: China–Egypt Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 21 April 1994, Beijing; FET, expropriation protection, free transfer, investor–state arbitration)
China–Egypt Double Taxation Agreement (signed 13 August 1997; in force and applied between the PRC State Taxation Administration and the Egyptian Tax Authority)
China–Egypt Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and Belt and Road Initiative economic cooperation framework (non-binding investment facilitation channel)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering (as amended by Laws No. 36/2014, No. 8/2015 and No. 154/2019); Executive Regulations per Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95 of 2016 (as amended); EMLCU (Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit) instructions; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT rules; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (UBO declarations to GAFI); Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; Egypt's obligations as MENAFATF member and FATF observer.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public Office, People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Hague Apostille not available because Egypt is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Apostille Convention): (i) PRC notarization; (ii) PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication; (iii) legalization by the Embassy of Egypt in Beijing

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018, particularly Articles 84-95 for Limited Liability Companies; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Article 8 and its Executive Regulations on One-Stop-Shop incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Incorporation Contract) submitted through the GAFI One-Stop Shop electronic platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an LLC; quota holders must subscribe the full capital and pay at least 25% of cash subscription up-front, with the balance payable within five years; all capital contributions must be deposited in a GAFI-supervised temporary bank escrow account prior to incorporation certification.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the quota holders present approve the subscription of the authorised capital and the constitution of the Company. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the address stated in the Articles, with the Manager authorised to execute the lease and register the official address. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the incorporators appoint [Name Surname] as Chief Executive Officer and Manager, [Name Surname] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name Surname] as Corporate Secretary, granting such officers full authority under the Companies Law to open bank accounts, sign filings, and commence licensing applications. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all actions taken in furtherance of incorporation are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve company name and obtain name clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the GAFI One-Stop Shop electronic portal and select 'New Company Formation' for an LLC. Submit three proposed Arabic names, each ending with 'LLC', in order of preference. Pay the name reservation fee online and obtain a preliminary naming certificate. Ensure the names do not violate public order, trademarks, or existing commercial register entries.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national ID copies of all quota holders
Power of attorney if submitting through an agent
GAFI name reservation application form
Signed undertaking of lawful business purposes
Evidence of capital contribution source if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity or conflict, file a written objection with the GAFI Legal Department within 30 days or submit revised alternative names; GAFI must issue a reasoned rejection that can be cured by renaming and re-reserving.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and notarize the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public / GAFI One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Egyptian lawyer or notary to prepare the Arabic-language Memorandum and Articles of Association specifying all quota holders, share distribution, registered office address, and management structure. All quota holders must appear personally or through a notarized power of attorney before the notary public to authenticate their signatures. Obtain a sealed notarized copy.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Rental contract or letter of intent for the registered office
Valid passports or national IDs of quota holders
Power of attorney on official stamp paper if representative acts
Name clearance certificate from GAFI
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the in-kind capital valuation, provide an independent valuation report or amend the contribution schedule; if the lease document is deficient, obtain a proper certified lease and resubmit to the same notary for re-authentication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit capital in an escrow bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow bank account at a GAFI-approved bank under the proposed company name. Deposit at least 25% of the cash capital subscription, or the entire in-kind contribution in physical or documentary form. Secure a bank deposit certificate explicitly stating the amount, date, account name, and purpose of the escrow.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (copy)
GAFI name clearance and registration file number
Passport copies of authorized signatories
Escrow deposit funding source declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the escrow account due to incomplete information, correct the KYC documentation or select another GAFI-approved bank; if the capital deposit certificate is disputed, request an immediate correction from the bank's operations department before submitting it to GAFI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit incorporation package and obtain commercial registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / Egyptian Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, bank escrow deposit certificate, lease contract for the registered office, and signed incorporation application through the GAFI OSS portal. GAFI electronically routes the application to the Egyptian Commercial Registry and the Tax Authority for simultaneous issuance of the commercial registration extract and tax card.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Rental contract and landlord authorization
GAFI incorporation application form
Power of attorney if used
Directors and manager acceptance letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the office scrutinizes inconsistencies, respond to the GAFI error note within 15 business days with corrected documents; for disputed capital allocations, provide bank statements or valuation certificates; once cured, GAFI resumes processing without restarting the full application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain tax registration, import-export code, and social insurance registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority / GAFI Foreign Trade Branch / National Organization for Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the GAFI OSS post-registration service to automatically generate the final tax identification number and commercial register extract. Separately apply to the GAFI Foreign Trade Branch for an importer/exporter code for the alcoholic beverage export business. Register all managers, shareholders active in the business, and employees with the National Organization for Social Insurance within 30 days.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration extract
Tax card and tax ID number
Company board resolution appointing officers
Passport copies of all personnel
Labor/work contracts for each engaged employee
Lease of warehouse or office
Commercial bank account confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is delayed due to file errors, make a written submission to the taxpayer services division and, if unresolved, escalate to the internal Tax Reconciliation Committee; for social insurance mismatches, align employment contracts and resubmit the list of insured persons.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt corporate seals, corporate books, and activate the bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / local Notary / company bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the commercial registration, procure a company seal bearing the exact registered Arabic name and commercial register number. Have the manager obtain a notarized specimen of the seal and signatures. Purchase and sequentially number the statutory minute book and share/quota register. Complete the bank account activation at the escrow bank by submitting the commercial registration, tax card, board resolution, and signature specimens, thereby converting the escrow into a fully operational corporate account.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate and tax card
Notarized board resolution on seal design and bank signatories
Corporate books purchase receipt and notary numbering certificate
Passport copies of bank authorized signatories
Company seal specimen form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the signature validity, obtain a GAFI-issued statement confirming the company's officers and re-submit the mandate; if corporate books are improperly numbered, present them to the notary for correction before the next annual assembly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) and the Local Governorate Economic Investment Administration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial and Commercial Operating License for Storage, Warehousing and Export Distribution of Alcoholic Beverages (الترخيص بمزاولة النشاط التجاري وفتح مخزن للتصدير)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Environmental Registration (Form EA-1); Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report not required unless storage capacity exceeds 1,000 metric tons annually or bottling/packaging operations are added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Prime Ministerial Decree No. 92 of 2013 for liquid waste: pH 6.5-9.0, BOD ≤ 600 mg/L, COD ≤ 1,000 mg/L, TSS ≤ 800 mg/L before discharge to public sewer; zero uncontrolled discharge to groundwater. Ethanol storage tanks must be equipped with vapor-recovery or equivalent VOC control achieving stack emissions below 150 mg/m³; hazardous waste including expired alcohol and contaminated containers must be transferred to EEAA-permitted waste handlers with delivery records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Authority fire safety certificate confirming installation of fire extinguishers, hydrants, smoke/heat detectors, and unobstructed egress; local municipality structural load inspection for warehouse floors and shelving; Ministry of Manpower occupational health clearance verifying workplace ventilation, spill containment, eye-wash facilities, staff first-aid kits, and emergency response training.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Ministry of Finance; national portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing and e-receipt clearance portal: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC obtains its unified TIN through the ETA's integrated tax registration workflow: (1) submit the Unified Tax Registration Statement at the competent ETA tax office in the district of the registered office; (2) attach the legalised memorandum of association and trade registry extract, proof of office premises, board resolution appointing a local tax representative, statutory accounting records, and bank certificate evidencing the Egyptian corporate account; (3) a non-resident without a permanent establishment must appoint a licensed Egyptian fiscal representative. The ETA issues a single electronic tax card containing the TIN/VAT registration number; the taxpayer must then activate its e-invoicing account and obtain the digital stamping/QR-signing credentials before issuing any commercial invoice.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Egyptian LLC is a tax-resident juridical person taxed in Egypt on worldwide income at the standard corporate income tax rate; no pass-through status is available to corporate members.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election exists under Egyptian law, and hybrid mismatch treatment is regulated by BEPS Action 2-aligned anti-hybrid provisions without a free-form election. Available elected regimes include: (a) SME presumptive CIT on annual revenue under Law No. 22 of 2023 at progressive rates from 0% up to 15% for turnovers up to EGP 100 million, elected in lieu of the standard 22.5% accounting-based tax; (b) special investment-incentive schedules and periodic CIT exemptions for licensed SCZone and Golden License enterprises under Law 83/2002 and Investment Law 72/2017; (c) cash-basis accounting election for eligible small taxpayers; (d) formal fiscal-representative election by non-resident taxpayers for VAT and withholding purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) — Law No. 67 of 2016 and its Executive Regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration applies to any taxable person whose annual value of taxable supplies exceeds EGP 500,000 (Art. 15, VAT Law 67/2016); non-resident suppliers of digital and electronic services are subject to compulsory registration regardless of threshold through an Egyptian fiscal representative.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: A phased national mandate now covers all ETA-registered taxpayers: every B2B/B2G case invoice and applicable B2C e-receipt must be transmitted in ETA-compliant XML/JSON to the national clearance portal (https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg), pass real-time schema, VAT-ratio, counterparty-eligibility and anti-fraud validation, and receive an ETA-issued UUID, QR code and digital stamp before being recognised for the buyer's input-VAT deduction. The exporting LLC must maintain an API-enabled e-invoicing account, digital signing certificate and structured counterparty acceptance/rejection workflow; invoices lacking ETA clearance are treated as not issued for tax purposes, attract per-invoice fines typically ranging from EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000, and can trigger tax-card suspension.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods, including Chinese baijiu spirits, are zero-rated under Art. 11 of VAT Law 67/2016 where: (a) the goods physically leave Egypt through an approved export port within the statutory shipment window; (b) the customs export declaration names the EG LLC as exporter; (c) ownership passes to a non-resident buyer under a duly executed sale contract; and (d) the sales proceeds are received through an Egyptian Authorised Dealer bank in freely convertible foreign currency. Ancillary freight, handling, insurance and commission services supplied for the exported goods are also zero-rated. The exporter recovers attributable input VAT through the streamlined ETA export-refund mechanism, subject to substantive verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bayan Jumruki) carrying the ETA and customs exit certification
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing lawful outbound shipment from Egyptian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency credit advice issued by the Egyptian Authorised Dealer bank
Commercial invoice, packing list, and signed sales contract/purchase order correlated line-by-line with the customs declaration
Letter of Credit or SWIFT payment instruments and beneficial-owner/export declaration for AML and fiscal cross-verification
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA automatically cross-matches customs exit data, e-invoiced VAT returns and Central Bank of Egypt FX-flow records to verify real export substance. If zero-rating lacks the required documentation or hard-currency proceeds are not credited to the Egyptian bank account within the 180-day repatriation deadline (or an approved extension), the ETA retroactively assesses VAT at 14% on the invoice value, adds monthly delay penalties of 0.5% of the assessed tax, and imposes fines of 30%–100% of the under-declared tax. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims constitute VAT-evasion offences punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years, full clawback of refunds, customs criminal liability, disqualification of the managing officers, and suspension or blacklisting of the exporter in the ETA tax-card, customs broker and foreign-trade operator registers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — Foreign Exchange, Banking Operations, and External Trade Compliance Directorate
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed floating exchange rate regime for the Egyptian Pound (EGP). Current and capital account operations are largely liberalized through CBE-licensed banks, and the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 guarantees repatriation of invested capital and profits. Practical convertibility hurdles include mandatory CBE reporting, economic substance disclosures, tax clearance certificates, delayed FX availability during periods of liquidity stress, and restrictive documentary scrutiny on remittance purposes. Profit remittance is permissible for Egyptian LLCs provided that audited financial statements, corporate tax clearance, and a board-authorized remittance resolution are presented to the maintaining bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE external trade instructions, all export proceeds must be repatriated to Egypt and credited to the exporter's Egyptian bank account within six months from the date of the underlying shipping declaration. There is no fixed mandatory conversion percentage under the current managed float; exporters may retain foreign currency revenue in approved foreign-currency accounts, but the CBE retains authority to impose, by circular, dedicated conversion ratios or temporary surrender obligations to support foreign exchange reserves. For alcoholic beverages such as Chinese baijiu, the exporter must submit the customs export declaration, CBE receipt statement, and original shipping documents as proof of performance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Trade Finance Operational Account / Foreign Currency Account
Operational Account / Import Export Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility rating: Egyptian law restricts full banking, e-money, and foreign exchange services to institutions licensed or expressly recognized by the CBE. Offshore fintech/EMI platforms (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business, neobank platforms) cannot lawfully hold Egyptian clearing accounts, open local EGP accounts, or act as the primary liquidity settlement rail for an Egyptian treasury. They may be used strictly as ancillary invoicing and foreign-currency collection tools for international customers, provided no local EGP clearing takes part in the collection flow; the core compliance-cleared USD settlement must be executed through a physical Egyptian licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Egyptian tier-1 banks require at least one physical visit to the branch for the company's legal representative and one ultimate beneficial owner holding at least 25% of the capital. The KYC interview is conducted in person by the compliance officer, and biometric or visual identification is mandatory. Remote digital onboarding is generally not accepted for non-resident directors. Where a foreign director is unable to travel, a notarized and apostilled/consular-legalized power of attorney addressed to an Egyptian resident authorized signatory may be accepted after the initial in-person interview of the in-country signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign Chinese individuals and opaque corporate chains appearing as shareholders/beneficial owners of the Egyptian LLC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Egyptian-Arabic translated and legalized certificate of beneficial ownership; full organizational chart traced to ultimate natural persons; passport and national ID copies of shareholders; board resolution appointing the Egyptian general manager and authorized signatories; GAFI investment certificate; vendor/director AML questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for initial capital injection and potential funding of the LLC's capital escrow account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six-months original bank statements of the sending parent company; audited financial statements; signed memoranda of association for the Egyptian LLC; evidence of the share capital financing wire; source of wealth declaration signed by the investor; tax receipts or tax status certificates from the foreign jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory scrutiny of an alcohol-export scope, including licensing and import/export compliance for high-proof Chinese baijiu
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial register listing approved ISIC 4632 activity; import/export registration card issued by the General Organization for Import and Export Control; Ministry of Trade and Industry approval for alcoholic-beverage distribution (where applicable); customs HS 2208.90 classification and product compliance documentation; CAIQ/product safety certificates from the Chinese exporter; any required Egyptian Ministry of Interior alcohol-related permits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border payments to Chinese suppliers and risk of mis-invoicing, transfer pricing, or sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed backend purchase contracts and supplier pro forma invoices; Bill of Lading and packing list; Chinese export customs declarations; bank settlement reports; OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening results of all parties; internal written transfer-pricing and trade-compliance policy; corporate foreign payment forecast and board-approved treasury mandate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Chinese sponsors must wire the equity capital via a SWIFT MT103 from the parent corporate bank account to the Egyptian LLC's CBE-supervised capital escrow and operational account. The incoming wire instruction must clearly quote the CBE balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment in Egyptian LLCs, i.e., 'FDI — Equity Capital Participation.' The Egyptian bank will verify the GAFI investment file, the LLC's capital structure, the beneficial ownership register, and the prospect of an audited baseline. The funds must be reflected in the CBE's external position reporting within one business day; the LLC must preserve all SWIFT acknowledgments, remittance advices, and bank conversion receipts to support subsequent profit repatriation and tax basis.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments for procurement of Chinese baijiu inventories are executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 direct credit wires for prepayment and open-account settlement, and via irrevocable documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) at sight for large consignments. Any import payment register must be enforced against the Egyptian NAFEZA Single Window import declaration; the disbursement account must maintain matching USD liquidity. For export-related third-party service payments, use the company's foreign-currency account with the maintaining Egyptian bank and ensure each outward transfer is accompanied by a supplier invoice, contract, and relevant customs or logistics evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CBE-authorized onshore deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for genuine trade-hedging exposure, typically executed against underlying import/export invoices and limited to a maximum tenor of 12 months
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with offshore banking counterparties permitted only as external non-EGP synthetic hedges, structured so no EGP conversion at maturity occurs onshore
Cross-currency swaps with Egyptian authorized dealing banks where the hedge aligns with underlying trade receivables in USD and EGP operating expenditures
Plain-vanilla FX options through Egyptian licensed banks for transaction-specific downside protection, subject to CBE confirmation of the corporate treasury mandate and underlying commercial risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Register Office, Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade, acting through the GAFI consolidated electronic company-services portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through January 31 of each calendar year for companies whose registration existed on December 31; newly registered entities renew in the anniversary month of the original registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal fine of EGP 100 per month applied from February 1; continued failure to renew for five consecutive years triggers administrative erasure from the Commercial Register and prohibition of the LLC from lawfully conducting business

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general assembly approval package with audited financial statements, auditor's report, and approved partners' resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year-end, i.e., by June 30 for a December 31 year-end; the partners' assembly must approve the financial statements before filing; GAFI filing submitted within 15 days of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EGP 5,000 to EGP 20,000 under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 for failure to convene or file the annual assembly; two consecutive years of non-filing may result in a GAFI petition for judicial strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 41) attaching audited financial statements and export-invoice schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), competent tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of the fiscal year-end, i.e., by April 30 for a December 31 year-end; no extension available in the general case
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of up to 10% of the declared tax liability with an EGP 500 minimum; monthly late-payment supplement of 2% of the unpaid tax; non-submission of audited statements may trigger a forced assessment, comprehensive tax audit, and personal collection exposure of the manager

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-ownership (UBO) register confirmation and change-of-ownership update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Companies Register and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) inspection framework
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation filed together with the GAFI annual financial statement package by June 30; any transfer of quotas or change of beneficial ownership registered within 30 days of the notarized transfer deed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EGP 50,000 up to EGP 500,000 under Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 for failure to register or update UBO data; suspension of the GAFI license and criminal liability of managers for willful omission

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based exemption applies: every Egyptian LLC under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 must appoint at least one auditor registered with the Egyptian Tax Authority, irrespective of turnover, assets, or employees; export license holders under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 must additionally maintain audited statements in support of VAT export zero-rating and customs duty drawback procedures
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued by the Ministry of Finance and substantially converged with IFRS; statutory books and financial statements must be maintained in Arabic, with audited English translations when used for foreign-bank remittance or credit purposes

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain an internal UBO ledger identifying any natural person directly or indirectly owning or controlling 25% or more of capital or voting rights, plus any ultimate controlling person; quota transfers in an LLC require a notarized deed followed by registration of the new quota allocation with the Commercial Register/GAFI within 30 days; the annual confirmation accompanying the June 30 GAFI filing must attest that the UBO ledger is current and accurate
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – 1,500 per year for a Cairo or Alexandria fiduciary registered-office and compliance-agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 – 2,500 per year for a small-to-mid-sized spirits-export LLC; higher for complex intercompany financing and foreign-payment transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, a company licensed to operate inside a designated free zone such as the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) is exempt from the standard corporate income tax and instead pays an annual 1% tax on the value of goods entering and leaving the free zone; this can apply to an export-oriented Baijiu repackaging and distribution LLC if the goods do not enter Egyptian customs territory. For non-free-zone exporters, no generalized alcohol-industry tax holiday exists, but GAFI-approved new or expanded export projects may claim an incentive deduction of up to 50% of taxable profit for the first five years, subject to substance and export earnings criteria. Export proceeds repatriated through Egyptian banks are eligible for standard commercial deductions, but there is no separate exemption specifically for spirits distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 114 – Corporate Income Tax Return; filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal with authenticated signature and mandatory TP declaration attachment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance tax declarations may be required for taxpayers classified as Large Taxpayers by the ETA
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months following the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year LLC, no later than April 30 of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identity: name of the LLC, commercial registry number, Egyptian tax card number, and seat address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Egyptian tax card issued by the ETA and the GAFI commercial registration certificate; no foreign parent identification should be substituted for the Egyptian national identity fields.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period and tax year-end date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the fiscal year-end approved in the Articles of Association; if the foreign parent operates on a calendar year, do not automatically align the Egyptian company's year-end without ETA prior approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross receipts including export sales revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert all revenue from Chinese Baijiu export sales into EGP using the Central Bank of Egypt official exchange rate as of the transaction date; attach Bills of Lading, S.W.I.F.T. wire advices or Letter of Credit records supporting each export invoice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit before exemption, loss relief, and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the profit to certified Egyptian books; apply all transfer pricing adjustments before entering this line; if the LLC is free-zone licensed, complete the supplementary free-zone declaration instead of entering full CIT base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax credits, foreign tax credits, and DTA relief relied upon
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach withholding tax certificates, the Chinese Tax Residency Certificate, and a draft Electronic Tax Form summarizing foreign-source taxable income; claims without TRC evidence are administratively refused.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative fine under the Tax Procedures Law No. 174 of 2018, generally between EGP 500 and EGP 100,000, plus a monthly late penalty of 5% of the net tax due, capped at 40% of the tax. Delay interest at the Central Bank of Egypt credit rate plus 2% accrues on unpaid balances. Failure to submit the transfer pricing declaration or Local/Master File carries a separate penalty of approximately EGP 30,000 per omitted document. No per-diem daily surcharge is used; penalties are assessed on a monthly basis.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% of gross dividend distributions payable to non-resident shareholders under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, unless a reduced rate is available under an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Egyptian LLC must file a reduced withholding request with the ETA International Tax Centre before distributing the dividend. The file must include: (i) a current-year Tax Residency Certificate issued by the Chinese State Taxation Administration; (ii) a beneficial ownership declaration confirming the Chinese shareholder is not acting as a conduit; (iii) a copy of the Articles of Association, share register, and proof of direct shareholding; and (iv) evidence of continued economic substance in China. ETA approval may be structured as annual clearance; upon approval the dividend WHT is reduced to the treaty rate at the time of payment. Excess WHT may be reclaimed by way of an ETA refund application if not reduced at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates are 20% for interest and 20% for royalty payments to non-residents. Under the Egypt-China DTA, the rates are generally capped at 10% for both interest and royalties, provided the beneficial owner submits a valid Chinese Tax Residency Certificate and the payments are not attributable to a permanent establishment in Egypt. The DTA relief is denied if the recipient entity lacks substantive ownership or control, or if the arrangement is an artificial profit-shifting conduit.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Transfer Pricing Local File is required where annual controlled transactions with a single related party exceed EGP 15,000,000, or when the Egyptian taxpayer has gross revenue exceeding EGP 30,000,000 and controlled transactions exceed EGP 5,000,000. A Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated global revenue exceeds EGP 100,000,000; Country-by-Country reporting thresholds apply separately under ETA decree.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: There is no codified Economic Substance Regulation identical to the UAE ESR regime. However, by virtue of Article 33 of the Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 and the Tax Procedures Law No. 174 of 2018, the ETA applies a robust substance-over-form and GAAR analysis. A Baijiu export LLC must maintain real premises, personnel, logistics contracts, supplier and customer files, board minutes, bank accounts, and decision-making records in Egypt. Where staff and management are effectively located abroad, the ETA may disregard the Egyptian entity as artificial, re-allocation profits to the foreign parent or treating the Egyptian LLC as a permanent establishment of a foreign principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating Baijiu export revenue, issuing or using forged Bills of Lading, creating parallel cash sales, or overstating export commissions paid to related parties solely to conceal taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the evaded tax at 150% of the under-declared amount; criminal fine of up to EGP 500,000 and imprisonment for a term not less than five years under Article 89 of Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended; revocation of the tax card and customs export registration; seizure of goods and bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts routinely pierce the corporate veil in fraud cases: directors and finance officers are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax plus penalties, their personal assets may be attached, and travel bans are issued during criminal investigation or enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Sham Transfer Pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Utilizing a foreign shell entity without employees, premises, or functions to route revenues or pay inflated royalties and commissions; creating circular financing or artificial margins that strip profit from the Egyptian LLC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA disallows the contract under the general anti-abuse rule, recharacterizes the transaction, and recalculates the Egyptian taxable profit at 22.5%; additional 20% withholding tax on deemed service or royalty flows may apply; monthly late penalty of 5% up to 40% is added. Criminal filing of false declarations also subjects the entity to fines of EGP 200,000 up to EGP 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve the false transfer pricing declaration face personal civil liability for the additional corporate tax, disqualification from board service in Egypt, and criminal liability for submitting false official statements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using over-invoicing, under-invoicing, deliberately obscured S.W.I.F.T. wire instructions, cash structuring, false commodity descriptions, or routing payments to or from sanctioned jurisdictions in relation to Baijiu export transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of Egypt AML Law No. 80 of 2002 attract criminal fines up to EGP 2,000,000 and imprisonment up to ten years, as well as asset freezing and confiscation. The Ministry of Investment may suspend, revoke, or refuse the commercial license and export privileges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and the Compliance Officer may be held personally and criminally liable where negligence or knowledge is proven; civil third-party liability is unlimited and travel bans are imposed to guarantee presence during investigation and restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unreported Cross-Border Dividends, Interest, and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to foreign shareholders or making interest and royalty payments without applying the applicable 10% dividend WHT or 20% interest/royalty WHT, and without obtaining prior ETA approval for the reduced treaty rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA will assess the unpaid withholding tax, impose a delay surcharge, and add a non-compliance fine that may reach 100% of the withheld amount. The underlying payment may be disallowed as a deductible expense in the Egyptian corporation's tax calculation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized the non-whthheld remittance become personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax and fines; the corporate veil is pierced to recover the amount from the directors' personal bank accounts, and a personal travel ban can be issued until full settlement.
